definition: Strenuous means requiring great physical energy and stamina.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word strenuous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know strenuous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Moving day proved more strenuous than the couple expected; by noon the stairs had beaten them, and they hired two teenagers to finish the job.
A brisk walk raises your heart rate pleasantly; strenuous effort makes real demands on muscle and breath.
Punishing goes beyond strenuous: a strenuous climb taxes your strength, while a punishing one damages it, leaving the body wrecked for days.

Exhausting means draining all your energy, of any kind — a day of interviews or grief can be exhausting without your lifting a thing. Strenuous is narrower: it names what a task demands of muscle and stamina, not what it leaves behind. A strenuous climb taxes the legs; an exhausting week can empty you at a desk.

Demanding says a task asks a great deal, and it does not care of what — patience, brainpower, or sweat. Strenuous pins the demand to the body: great physical energy and stamina spent in the doing. A proof can be demanding from an armchair; nothing is strenuous from an armchair.

Strenuous entered English in the 1500s from Latin strenuus, 'active, eager.' Theodore Roosevelt made it famous preaching 'the strenuous life,' but the root never produced another common English word, so this one stands alone.
Strenuous means requiring great physical energy and stamina.
The scallop divers' season is short and strenuous: forty pounds of gear, four dives a day, and currents that fight every kick.
Rookies assume swimming skill will carry them; by the second week, most discover that no gym could have readied their legs and lungs.
Strenuous keeps its focus on the body: a strenuous task demands muscle power and stamina, whatever else it asks.
Homework can be hard, but only the paper route is strenuous.
Strenuous is the body's word: use it when the cost is muscle, breath, and stamina.
Arduous covers difficulty and tiredness of any kind, and laborious the long slow grind; vigorous - also in this unit - describes the energy someone brings, not the energy a task demands.
A vigorous swimmer enjoys a strenuous workout.

The volunteer crew spent June rebuilding the washed-out trail below the summit ridge.
Mornings began with paperwork - permits, sign-in sheets, a safety talk that never changed.
The strenuous part came after: hauling ninety-pound stones uphill in slings, two volunteers to a stone, lungs burning in the thin air.
By the third week, veterans could tell newcomers by their legs, which quivered on the evening walk back to camp.
Yet nobody quit, and the finished staircase now carries four thousand hikers a summer.
